comments.author: angrizan 0.
comments.comment: The hard part is not adding a harness, it is keeping the action surface small enough that agents do not turn every DOM path into a tool. I’d want each site to expose intent-level operations, clear failure modes, and eval traces for what the agent tried, not just a bigger browser API.

comments.author: Anuj Kumar Sharma
comments.comment: The hardest jump is usually not RAG or agents, it is learning how to measure failure before users find it. A strong AI engineer should be able to define eval sets, latency budgets, fallback paths, and ownership boundaries before writing the first prompt. Curious how much of the cohort is hands-on debugging of broken AI systems versus building the happy path.

comments.author: Christian Raae
comments.comment: The underrated part is the per-project context contract. Once the agent has stable project memory, tool permissions, and a clear approval boundary, the workflow shifts from “chat with a model” to “delegate a repeatable operating loop.” I’d be curious how you handle failure modes - do you log every agent action for review, or only the ones that touched external systems?
